QuestionStmt.S: 5 g urea is dissolved in 100 g water. Find the amount of glucose to be dissolved in 120 g of water so that the boiling points of both solutions will be the same. [Molar mass of urea = 60 g mol⁻¹ & Molar mass of glucose = 180 g mol⁻¹]

Solution.S:
Step 1: For boiling points to be the same, the molality of both solutions must be equal (since both are non-electrolytes).

Step 2: Molality of urea solution = (5 g / 60 g/mol) / (100 g / 1000 g/kg) = (0.0833 mol) / 0.1 kg = 0.833 m.

Step 3: Let mass of glucose be $w$ g. Moles of glucose = $w/180$.

Step 4: Molality of glucose solution = $(w/180)$ / (120 g / 1000 g/kg) = $(w/180)$ / 0.12 = $w / (180 × 0.12) = w / 21.6$.

Step 5: Set molalities equal: $0.833 = w / 21.6$ ⇒ $w = 0.833 × 21.6 = 18$ g.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{18 \text{ g}}$$

Hence, the correct option is C.
